Can you confirm:

2) Redwood Private (VPC) deployment lead time and on-prem hardware procurement lead time if we take that path?
3) Sizing guidance for initial staging pool vs a production committed pool to meet the above throughput targets (assume 99th pct latency target 300ms)?

Appreciate a short MAP draft this week so procurement can start internal approvals.

Thanks,

Hi Sara / team —

I put together a sizing sketch and a few test-run observations (see attached gpu_sizing_model_runs.csv). High level: your stress runs (~180 rps) are a good signal, but we use concurrency and token-rate to size a pool. Below is a conservative recommendation that balances cost and latency for the 99th percentile ~300ms target you mentioned.

Assumptions used for sizing:
- Model: open LLM (medium ~30B), optimized runtimes; typical token throughput per GPU = ~1.8k tokens/sec for A100-80GB under continuous batching in our tests (your workload mix will change this).
- Typical request profile: input + output ~80 tokens total (short completion focus)
- Observed peak RPS: 180 rps (from your test)

Quick math (rounded):
- Token rate at 180 rps * 80 tokens = 14,400 tokens/sec required.
- At 1.8k tokens/sec per A100-80GB -> ~8 GPUs to cover token throughput headroom (~8 x A100-80GB).

Recommendation (phased):
- Staging (acceptance tests, canaries): 6–8 x A100-40/80GB (we typically recommend 40GB for staging to cut cost, but if you plan memory-heavy prompts use 80GB).
- Canary / early prod: 12 x A100-80GB (handles burst and allows headroom for autoscaling).
- Committed prod reserve: 24 x A100-80GB for a strong runway (handles sustained growth and provides failover capacity).

Alternative cheaper stack (if cost-sensitive): use A10s for staging (10–12x A10) and then move to A100s for prod commit. If you expect long-running batch jobs (many tokens) increase prod pool by ~25%.

Lead-time notes we should add to the MAP:
- Dedicated: 6–8 weeks typical; can be 3–4 weeks if we mark "expedite" and inventory is available in region.
- Private (managed VPC): 8–12 weeks (network clearance / IP allowlists add time).
- On-prem procurement: vendor-dependent ~12–16 weeks for hardware + rack/cabling + site acceptance testing.

Operational suggestions:
- Start with a 6–8 GPU staging pool in December to run acceptance tests and regression evals.
- Keep a 12 GPU canary for the first month of production to validate traffic shaping and rollback policies.
- Use model-variant fallback chains in the MAP (e.g., fallback to quantized variant) to reduce cost during spikes.

I attached the CSV with sample run logs and the spreadsheet will include our calculated numbers. Happy to walk through the math on a short call.

— Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Capacity Planning — Redwood Inference

Team —

Thanks — below is a concise MAP summary and concrete next steps so procurement can close gating by mid-December. I attached a draft MOU (nexa_mou_draft.pdf) and our updated MAP spreadsheet (nexa_map_v1.xlsx) with the dates filled.

MAP summary (milestones & dates) — target schedule
- LOI / MOU signed (soft reserve): target by 2026-12-10
- Legal review / MSA negotiation: target complete by 2026-12-20 (we typically execute SOW after MSA)
- Staging reservation (soft provision): start 2027-01-10 (6–8 GPUs for acceptance)
- Canary: 2027-01-24 (12 GPUs, traffic split)
- Prod commit / reserved pool provisioning (Dedicated): provision by 2027-03-01 (target 24 x A100-80GB)

Commercial answers (short):
- We will provide a redline-ready MSA and SOW template. Standard payment terms offered: Net30. Longer terms available by exception (Net45) — please flag if you need Net45.
- Private (managed VPC): Redwood manages orchestration; you do not need to purchase on-prem hardware unless you explicitly choose on-prem air-gapped deployment. Gating items that can extend timelines: IP allowlist approvals, network ACL reviews, and any customer-side security hardening (usually 1–3 weeks additional if not prioritized).
- Expedited Dedicated provisioning: available; inventory-dependent. Expedited provisioning may carry an uplift. We will mark an expedite path in the quote and note the optional fee.

Sizing summary (from our tests):
- Staging: 6–8 x A100 (40GB or 80GB depending on memory) — start Jan 10, 2027
- Canary: 12 x A100-80GB — Jan 24, 2027
- Prod reserved commit: 24 x A100-80GB — provision goal Mar 1, 2027

Fallback / operational controls:
- We will include canary to prod rollout controls, automatic fallback to quantized model variants, and a multi-region fallback (if desired) to keep service up while capacity comes online.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: review attached MOU and confirm if LOI sign by 2026-12-10 is acceptable. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/xyz/nexa-loi (placeholder).
2) Technical: please share final model family and average input token length so we can lock the exact GPU counts in the spreadsheet.
3) Commercial: confirm payment terms (Net30 / Net45) and whether you want expedite options included in initial quote.

I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff as soon as LOI is signed to run through acceptance criteria and SOC2 evidence paths.

— Lukas Meyer
